title: An Autumn Without a Date
reflection:
Trees do not consult a calendar before they let their leaves fall — only their own inward sense that the season has turned. Yours may turn less predictably now, arriving without the date you once expected it by.

Whatever this month's heaviness is, let it be autumn all the same, on its own irregular clock. The tree does not need to know exactly when to know it's time.
closing: Like the tree that sheds without a calendar, let me release on my body's own uncertain timing. I trust the bare branch. Amen.

scripture.text: To everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven.

title: A Fallower Field
reflection:
Some fields were once rested on a fixed rotation, one year in seven. Yours rests on no such schedule now — fallow when it needs to be fallow, unpredictably, and no less needed for its irregularity.

If today asks less of you than you expected, let the field lie fallow without apology. Rebuilding does not announce its own timetable.
closing: I am fallow ground, on whatever schedule my body chooses. Restore what only unscheduled rest can restore. Amen.

scripture.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside still waters.

title: Green Appearing Off-Season
reflection:
Every so often a plant blooms out of its usual season — startling, a little disorienting, entirely real. Your returns of energy may come the same way now: unscheduled, occasionally surprising you.

Don't distrust the green because it arrived at an unexpected time. Let it be exactly the renewal it is.
closing: Thank you for this off-season green. I receive it as real, whatever the calendar says about its timing. Amen.

scripture.text: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.

title: The Tide With No Table
reflection:
Once you could read a tide table and know exactly when the water would turn. Now the pull is real but its timing has slipped from any table you can consult.

The tide still turns. It has simply stopped announcing itself in advance. Rest in the not-yet the way the shore rests between one tide and the next — certain of the turning, uncertain only of the hour.
closing: Keep me steady between tides whose table I no longer have. I trust the pull, even unannounced. Amen.

scripture.text: But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.
